name: AP2171WG-7
title: AP2161 / AP2171: 1 A single-channel current-limited high-side power switch
summary: A single-channel high-side power switch for USB ports and hot-swap loads, running from 2.7 V to 5.5 V with a 95 mΩ switch and up to 1 A of continuous load. It limits current at 1.5 A typical, shuts down on over-temperature, blocks reverse current, ramps its output in about 0.6 ms and holds off below a 1.9 V undervoltage threshold. An open-drain FLG output reports over-current or over-temperature after a 7 ms blanking time. AP2161 has an active-low enable and AP2171 an active-high one; AP2161WG-7 is the AP2161 in SOT25 on 7-inch tape and reel.
key_figures: 95 mΩ typ, 115 mΩ max (VIN = 5 V, IOUT = 1 A, SOT25 / MSOP-8EP / SO-8); 90 mΩ typ U-DFN2018-6
1.1 A min, 1.5 A typ, 1.9 A max
4 ms min, 7 ms typ, 15 ms max
4 kV HBM; 400 V MM (MSOP-8EP, SOT25), 300 V MM (U-DFN2018-6, SO-8)

notes: Order code AP21X1 XX G -X: the digit after AP21 is 6 for active-low enable or 7 for active-high; 1 is one channel; the package code follows (W SOT25, S SO-8, MP MSOP-8EP, FM U-DFN2018-6); G marks the green compound; the suffix -7 or -13 is the reel size in inches.
On SO-8 and MSOP-8EP the top line reads AP21 then 8 (active low) or 9 (active high), then 1 for one channel. On SOT25 and U-DFN2018-6 the identification code is HT for AP2161 and HU for AP2171.

circuits.title: Typical application, AP2171 with active-high enable
circuits.description: An AP2171 connects a 2.7 V to 5.5 V supply to a load. On the supply side a polarised 10 µF and a 0.1 µF go to ground; on the output a 0.1 µF and a polarised 120 µF go to ground. FLG is open-drain and is pulled up to the supply through 10 kΩ; the same node leaves as the fault signal. EN is switched between on (high) and off (low).

circuits.title: One-port USB host or self-powered hub
circuits.description: An AP2161 connects a 5 V supply to VBUS of a downstream USB port. IN has 0.1 µF to ground; VBUS has 0.1 µF and 120 µF to ground. A USB controller drives EN and reads FLG, which is pulled up to a 3.3 V supply through a resistor. The port's D+ and D- lines enter from the left with no part on them.

where.PD: total power dissipated in the switch
where.RDS(ON): switch on-resistance at the highest ambient temperature

operation.text: IN wants a 0.01 µF to 0.1 µF ceramic (X7R or X5R) to GND, placed close. When the load is heavy, an electrolytic of 10 µF or more is recommended on IN and on OUT to reduce supply transients and ringing at the input. A 0.01 µF to 0.1 µF ceramic on OUT improves immunity to short-circuit transients.

Current is measured by a sense FET, so no resistor adds to the path. In over-current the part holds the output current constant and lets the output voltage fall; it turns fully off only if the fault lasts until thermal limiting acts.

Output already shorted when the part is enabled or powered: ILIMIT applies at once. Short or overload while on: a brief higher current flows before the limit reacts, then the current is held at ILIMIT. Load rising slowly past the rated current: current climbs to the trigger threshold ITRIG (or until thermal limit) without harm, then the part falls back to ILIMIT.

Below -30 °C, an output short calls for at least 120 µF of electrolytic capacitance on OUT. The capacitor's voltage rating and type should keep its capacitance change under 10 % at the cold extreme; the aluminium electrolytic recommended is the Panasonic FC series.

FLG goes low after a 7 ms nominal deglitch when an over-current or over-temperature shutdown occurs and stays low until both have cleared. A brief over-current from charging a large output capacitance is shorter than the deglitch and does not set FLG, so no external filter is needed.

The die temperature is monitored. Near +145 °C, reached in a lasting overload or short, the switch turns off; it turns back on after the die has cooled by roughly 25 °C, and keeps cycling until the fault or the supply is removed. FLG is asserted, with the 7 ms deglitch.

The switch stays off, even when enabled, until IN reaches at least 1.9 V, and turns off quickly when IN drops below about 1.9 V. This suits hot-insertion systems where the switch cannot be turned off before power goes away.

A host or self-powered hub feeds its downstream ports from a local supply that must hold 4.75 V to 5.25 V at the port connector, on the board, at full and zero load. It must limit port current and report over-current to the USB controller. Examples include desktop computers, monitors, printers and standalone hubs.

Placed between the incoming VCC and the rest of a plug-in card, the switch is the first thing powered on insertion. Its controlled rise and fall (rise of about 1 ms typical) ramp the card's supply slowly, limiting the surge on the main supply, and UVLO keeps it off after removal and through the next insertion.

Every IN pin is joined to the others outside the package, and every OUT pin likewise. NC has no internal connection and is best tied to OUT. The exposed pad of MSOP-8EP and U-DFN2018-6 goes to GND and to thermal copper but does not serve as the ground current path.

ESD protection is 4 kV HBM and 300 V MM. The part is UL recognised (file E322375) and certified under the IEC60950-1 CB scheme. All packages use a green moulding compound: lead-free, RoHS compliant, halogen and antimony free.
